data.why: The dashboard needs no uploads; it generates dungeons from a seed, runs built-in PPO policies, and reads example results (results/showcase, results/ablation, results/comparison) already committed in the repository.

goals: Compare how feed-forward (MLP), short-history, GRU and LSTM PPO policies solve partially observable dungeon navigation tasks
Step or auto-run an agent through a seeded dungeon and watch its local observation, event trace and hidden-state evolve decision by decision
Fork a live episode and apply a controlled memory intervention (reset, partial zero, Gaussian noise, or restore) to isolate the causal effect of retained state on escape success
Replay the recorded, verified memory-deletion showcase (GRU, seed 200001) to see the control vs. treatment action divergence and final outcome
Inspect recorded experiment results (success rates, training curves, generalization and ablation tables/plots) across architectures and dungeon configurations
Vary dungeon seed, detour length, grid size and clue reliability to probe generalization and memory demand

review.summary: The tree describes the interface well: setup, step-through observation, fork-and-compare memory interventions and recorded results, with an appropriate depth and screens that support every node I checked. It needs fixes before filing: it leaves out the observation and event-trace view of the vanishing cue that the research question depends on, it wrongly says the results tab shows per-family ablation plots, and it calls the verified-deletion button a replay when it re-runs the recorded setup with whatever policy is loaded.
